_note: Combat parity fixture (01-08): five independent scenarios, each its own seed + forced encounter, so every outcome (win/lose/flee/parley) is deterministic and reachable in a small, fixed action count. `startCombat` is NOT in engine/actions.js's validated ACTION_TYPES (it is an internal function other rule domains call, not a player-facing action) -- test/parity/combat-parity.test.js special-cases it, calling engine/combat.js's startCombat directly (state/rng managed the same way applyAction does) and the prototype's `ctx.startCombat(wandering, forced)` directly, exactly mirroring the encounter the wandering-monster check or an encounter dot would eventually trigger. Every scenario's seed was found by a throwaway discovery script that simulated the engine directly against a forced encounter type until it produced the desired outcome (same method 01-05/01-07 used for chargen/movement fixture seeds), then cross-checked for prototype parity before being committed here. Phase 24 (2026-09-14, race pass, FID-07): `lose`'s seed-14 Fridgian Soldier now carries a declared `divergence` (kind action-path) — the frenzy corpse-whiff removal + hide -2 flip its outcome from died to won, measured live and asserted via test/parity/harness/comparables.js's actionPathDivergenceOf/skipsByteDiffAt/declaredEndDiffs; the new `lose-apprentice` scenario (seed 127, a plain Human, unaffected by the race pass) restores byte-identical death-path coverage.

divergence.rationale: This seed's hero is a Fridgian Soldier. From action 1 (the first attack) onward the prototype and engine diverge byte-for-byte because a Fridgian's hide (content/races.js, Phase 24) now soaks 2 flat from every landed foe blow, floor 1, stacking with Hardiness -- a pure damage-arithmetic change with zero rng-draw impact. Separately, the frenzy corpse-whiff branch (rng.d(10) against a dead foe, wasting both swings) was deliberately removed, since it never should have wasted the hero's second swing on a corpse in the first place -- this REMOVES exactly one rng.d(10) draw the first time this Fridgian frenzies with a dead foe present (action 7 of this scenario), shifting the rng cursor for every subsequent draw. The combined effect: the hero kills the Shriek at action 8 (engine) instead of dying to it at action 10 (prototype) -- the action path itself changes, not merely a numeric drift, so the per-action byte diff is skipped from action 1 onward and both sides' end-of-scenario c-fields (wp/sp/kills/rations) plus the dead flag are machine-checked against the measured before/after above instead. Neither the seed nor the action list were touched -- lose-apprentice (seed 127) restores byte-identical death-path parity coverage.

Phase 27 (TUNE-06): Dante was demoted to tier 2 and the tier-1 Humans row is now Ned (wp 8, one swing a round) -- the first deliberate canon deviation of the v1.2 retune (docs/DIFFICULTY-RETUNE.md, v1.2 section). From action 0 (startCombat) the engine rolls Ned x2 where the frozen prototype rolls Dante x2, so the foe objects and every downstream draw differ; the parley outcome on each side is recorded here as measured. No other scenario in any fixture rolls a Humans encounter, so this is the only divergence the Dante change causes.
